newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs seen stable unless PPI shocks.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs seen stable unless PPI shocks.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds were seen holding on to gains they made on Tuesday unless U.S. producer price data due on Wednesday rekindled inflation fears.
The benchmark 10-year OLO yield ended at an unchanged 5.88 percent, slightly up from earlier lows, but the spread over Bunds came in from around 12 or 13 basis points to 10 or 11.
"We are nearly back to the levels of last Thursday," one trader said, noting the spread then was nine basis points.
Dealers said a tight Treasury exchange auction, at which just 20 million francs of OLO 15 (6.75 pct, May 1997) was swapped for OLO 21 (7.75 pct, December 2000) helped the up move.
"You cannot really say there was a short squeeze, but there was a bit of a scramble for paper as Bunds ticked up," one said.
"People were expecting more (from the Treasury)," he added.
One dealer said activity had been focused on the short end of the yield curve on rumours the Bundesbank might cut rates again before the end of the year.

Another said, however, the movement was in the middle of the curve, with the yield difference between five- and 10-year OLOs going rising to nearly 128 basis points from 125 as investors bought five-year paper.
"I think things will stay pretty stable now unless PPI tomorrow confirms what (U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan) was saying about inflation last week," one trader said.
U.S. producer rises are expected to have risen by around 0.3 percent month-on-month, or 2.9 percent year-on-year, in November. The data is due to be released at 1330 GMT,
Another said, however, if Bund futures broke 101.12 the OLO market would be pulled sharply higher.
